hypotheses.statement: For every integer $k\ge0$, every distortion-$D$ embedding of $\mathcal D_k$ into either $X$ or $B_\infty$ satisfies $$D^2\ge1+k/4.$$

Let $X$ be a Banach space, $R>0$, and let $(z_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ satisfy $\|x\pm z_i\|\le R$ with $\|z_i-z_j\|\ge\varepsilon>0$ for $i\ne j$. Every half-difference $w=(z_i-z_j)/2$ with $i\ne j$ satisfies $\|w\|\ge\varepsilon/2$ and $\|x\pm w\|\le R$. Fix $\eta>0$. The following two selections are available.*


1.  *Suppose $p$ has finite support, $\|p-x\|<\eta$, and $P$ is a bounded finite-rank coordinate projection satisfying $Pp=p$. There are distinct $i,j$ for which, with $w=(z_i-z_j)/2$ and $y=w-Pw$, $$\label{met:pair-errors}
     \|Pw\|<\eta,\quad
     \|y\|\ge\varepsilon/2-\eta,\quad
     \|p\|\ge\|x\|-\eta,\quad
    \|p\pm y\|\le R+2\eta.$$*

2.  *If $F$ is a closed finite-codimensional subspace, there are distinct $i,j$ whose half-difference satisfies $\operatorname{dist}(w,F)<\eta$. This selection requires no coordinate structure on $X$.

In the finite-height segment forest dual, every infinite $\varepsilon$-separated symmetric $R$-lens satisfies $$\label{met:joint-lens}
 \|x\|^2+\varepsilon^2/16\le R^2.$$ The same lens conclusion holds for the infinite-height closed coordinate span with its own segment-dual norm and finite-head approximation theorem.

Suppose $v,u\in c_{00}(T)$, $v=P_Av$, and $u=Q_Au$, where $A$ is finite and ancestral. There is $c=Q_Ac\in c_{00}(T)$ such that $$\label{dir:correction-cost}
 \rho(c)\le\rho(u),\qquad
 \rho(v+c+r u)^2\le\rho(v)^2+16\rho(u)^2
 \quad(r\in\{-1,1\}).$$
Every embedding of $\mathcal D_k$ into $X$ with distortion at most $D$ satisfies $k\le256D^2$.
Every noncontracting $D$-Lipschitz embedding of $\mathcal D_k$ into $X$ satisfies $D>\sqrt{k}/144$ for $k\ge1$.

For the real space $X$ defined by [dir:atomic:forest-norm], no finite $D$ has the following property: for every $k\ge1$ there are a map $f_k:\mathcal D_k\to X$ and a scalar $a_k>0$ such that $$a_k d_k(u,v)\le\|f_k(u)-f_k(v)\|_X\le D a_k d_k(u,v) \qquad(u,v\in\mathcal D_k).$$

Suppose a depth-$k$ embedding satisfies [dir:atomic:normalization]. For every $0<\eta<1/(4D)$ one can select a fair binary slope martingale $(M_i)_{i=0}^k$, nested finite ancestral sets $S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_k$, and a finitely valued random atom $Z$ supported in $S_k$, such that, with $E_i=\mathbb E[\,\cdot\mid\mathcal F_i]$ and $U_i=E_iZ=P_{S_k}M_i$, $$\label{dir:atomic:preparation-bounds} \|Q_{S_{i-1}}U_{i-1}\|<\eta,\qquad \|P_{S_i\setminus S_{i-1}}U_i\|\ge1/D-4\eta \quad(1\le i\le k).$$ The unprojected slopes also satisfy $\|Q_{S_i}M_i\|<\eta$ for $0\le i\le k$. Every $M_i$ and $U_i$ has norm at most one. The additional terminal sampling used to produce $Z$ is excluded from each $\mathcal F_i$, including $\mathcal F_k$.

If every infinite $\varepsilon$-separated symmetric $R$-lens satisfies $\|x\|^2\le R^2-b\varepsilon^2$ for some $b>0$, then every embedding [met:all-pairs] satisfies $D^2\ge1+4bk$. If instead [met:radial-lens] holds, then $$\label{met:additive-bound} k\le C^2D(D-1).$$

Assume the density and projection-family hypotheses of Proposition 10. Let $q\ge2$ and $c>0$. Suppose that for every admissible projection, every pure head–tail pair $p,y$, and every $R>0$, $$\|p\pm y\|\le R \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|p\|^2+cR^{2-q}\|y\|^q\le R^2.$$ Then every distortion-$D$ embedding of $\mathcal D_k$ satisfies $$ck\le D^{q-2}(D^2-1).$$

Assume the density and projection-family hypotheses of Proposition 10. Fix constants $a,b>0$. Suppose that for every admissible projection and every pure head–tail pair $p,y$, the following estimate holds for all $\lambda>0$: $$\max_\pm\|p\pm y\|\ge \frac{\|p\|+a\lambda\|y\|}{\sqrt{1+b\lambda^2}}.$$ Put $Q=\sqrt{1+b\lambda^2}$. For noncontracting diamond slopes bounded above by $D$, the stage suprema satisfy $$R_j\le Q R_{j+1}-a\lambda \le R_{j+1}-\bigl(a\lambda-(Q-1)D\bigr).$$ In particular, whenever $\Delta=a\lambda-(Q-1)D>0$, one has $1+k\Delta\le D$.

Fix $0<\alpha\le1$. Suppose some $0\le\rho<1$ has the following property: whenever $\|x\pm z_i\|\le1$ and $\|z_i-z_j\|\ge2\alpha$ for $i\ne j$, one has $\|x\|\le\rho$. An embedding with lower factor $\alpha$ and upper factor one must satisfy $$\label{met:backward-bound}
 \alpha\le\rho^k,$$ where the empty product $\rho^0$ is one.

Let $D\ge1$ and $\delta>0$. If $(1+\delta)^k>D$, every noncontracting embedding with upper factor $D$ has a parent edge all of whose child slopes have norm at most $(1+\delta)$ times its own slope norm. If, for every unit $u$, the enlarged lens $$M(u,\delta)=\{z:\max_\pm\|u\pm z\|\le1+\delta\}$$ contains no infinite $2/D$-separated family, then every such embedding satisfies $$\label{met:bridge:enlarged-depth}
 1\le \frac{D}{(1+\delta)^k}.$$

Let $P$ be bounded and finite rank, let $A\subset X$ be bounded, and let $b\ge0$ and $\varepsilon>0$. If $\|(I-P)v\|\le b$ for all $v\in A$, then $A$ contains no infinite $\varepsilon$-separated family when $2b<\varepsilon$. Consequently the following two inputs have different graph conclusions.*

1.  *Let $0<\delta<1$. For each $\|x\|>1-\delta$, suppose one such $P$ bounds by $b(\delta)$ the tails of every $v$ with $\|x\pm v\|\le1$. If $2b(\delta)<2/D$, backward contraction gives $D^{-1}\le(1-\delta)^k$.*

2.  *Let $\delta>0$. For every unit $x$, suppose one such $P$ bounds by $b(\delta)$ the tails of every $v$ with $\|x\pm v\|\le1+\delta$. If $2b(\delta)<2/D$, actual-child selection gives $D\ge(1+\delta)^k$.*

*The same conclusions hold when the bound is on the first endpoint of every pair with $(u+v)/2=x$: take $u,v\in B_X$ in case (1), and $u,v\in(1+\delta)B_X$ in case (2).

Assume the density and projection-family hypotheses of Proposition 10. Suppose that whenever admissible heads $P_n\in\mathcal P$ and vectors $p_n,y_n$ satisfy $$P_np_n=p_n,\qquad P_ny_n=0,\qquad \|p_n\pm y_n\|\le1,\qquad \|p_n\|\longrightarrow1,$$ one has $\|y_n\|\longrightarrow0$. The heads are allowed to vary with $n$. Then, for each $\varepsilon>0$, there is $0<\rho<1$ such that every infinite $\varepsilon$-separated symmetric unit lens has center norm at most $\rho$.

Suppose that for some $t>0$ and $g>0$, every unit vector $u\in X$ admits a closed finite-codimensional subspace $F_u$ such that $$y\in F_u,\quad\|y\|\ge t
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \max\{\|u+y\|,\|u-y\|\}\ge1+g.$$ If $D\ge1$ and $t\le1/(2D)$, every noncontracting embedding of $\mathcal D_k$ with upper factor $D$ satisfies $D\ge(1+g/2)^k$.

Assume the finite-codimensional hypothesis of Proposition 18. Consider a noncontracting embedding with upper factor $D\ge1$. If $t\le1/D$ and all child slopes of one parent have norm at most $L$, then $\|x\|\le L/(1+g)$. Consequently every depth-$k$ embedding with upper factor $D$ satisfies $1\le D/(1+g)^k$.

If a Banach space admits an equivalent asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex norm, then the family $(\mathcal D_k)_{k\ge0}$ does not embed into it with uniformly bounded distortion. Write $\operatorname{cof}(X)$ for the closed finite-codimensional linear subspaces of $X$. In infinite dimension, midpoint convexity may be expressed by positivity of the maximum modulus $$\label{met:bridge:max-modulus}
 \delta_N^{\max}(t)=
 \inf_{N(u)=1}\ 
 \sup_{F\in\operatorname{cof}(X)}\ 
 \inf_{\substack{y\in F\\N(y)=1}}
 \bigl(\max_\pm N(u\pm t y)-1\bigr)>0
 \qquad(0<t<1).$$

For every $0<\varepsilon\le2$ there is $\eta(\varepsilon)\in(0,1)$ such that $$N_J(x\pm z_j)\le1,
 \qquad N_J(z_j-z_l)\ge\varepsilon\quad(j\ne l)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 N_J(x)\le1-\eta(\varepsilon).$$ For $\varepsilon>2$ the hypotheses are impossible, so any $\eta(\varepsilon)\in(0,1)$ is admissible. An embedding of the depth-$k$ countably branching diamond into $X_J$ with distortion at most $D$ therefore satisfies $$\label{met:f:sum-depth}
 D^{-1}\le\bigl(1-\eta(2/D)\bigr)^k.$$

If the depth-$k$ countably branching diamond admits an embedding into $X_0$ with distortion at most $D\ge1$, then $$\label{met:f:zero-depth}
 k\le4608D^3(1-D^{-1}).$$
For the segment forest space $X$, every map satisfying [met:all-pairs] has $D^2\ge1+k/16$.
If a target satisfies [met:bridge:fixed-bound-input], every noncontracting embedding of $\mathcal D_k$ with upper factor $D$ obeys $$1+kc_D\le D.$$
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $0<\rho<1$ such that an infinite $\varepsilon$-separated symmetric unit lens in the segment forest space has center norm at most $\rho$.

evidence.quote: A symmetric midpoint estimate becomes a graph obstruction because each edge of a countably branching diamond has infinitely many replacement midpoints.

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive integer coefficients in {-3,-1,0,1,3} on five trees of at most four nodes; ancestral heads specified in the vectors; tail supported only on first exterior roots.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent enumeration of ancestor suffixes reconstructs the correction; exhaustive pairwise-disjoint segment families compute exact squared primal norms and re-check both signs.
